stem:
The diagram shows Irfan's electromagnet: a coil on an iron nail joined to a cell. Ends of the nail are labelled X and Y. A magnetic compass is held near end X; the north pole of the compass needle is attracted towards X.

Which claim about the poles is correct?

options.text: End X is a South pole and end Y is a North pole.
End X is a North pole and end Y is a South pole.
Both ends X and Y are North poles.
Both ends X and Y are South poles.

teacher.key_rationale: Unlike poles attract, so the compass north pole is attracted to a South pole at X. The other end Y must be North. Both ends cannot share the same pole.
teacher.figure_note: Electromagnet with ends X and Y; compass N attracted toward X.
